sub_scenario.family: negotiating scope commitments when project evidence is incomplete
sub_scenario.one_line: construction procurement adviser: authorize inspection before a rebuild decision

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the tender ledger and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The site dossier review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can approve a replacement order when the specification and quantities are final.
Is approving purchases generally difficult?
No, not when the scope is settled and the price basis is comparable.
Someone new shadowed me in the procurement room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the bid cycles into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The depot refurbishment dossier shows the roof photographs and a provisional materials list, but the intrusive inspection has not happened.
What does that leave uncertain?
The extent of damaged structure and the quantity that would need replacement.
I recently arranged a small site survey with a fixed two-day allowance.
Why was that straightforward?
The survey boundary, access dates, and output were written down.
I archived last cycle's notes on the site dossier and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The authority has earmarked funds for an inspection and can authorize a contractor visit this month.
Can that money cover the rebuild?
No, it is reserved for finding the condition behind the cladding.
A vendor call about the tender ledger ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the procurement room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the bid cycles.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the site dossier records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The facilities lead has booked the inspection window and agreed that its report will set the repair package before tendering.
What follows from that agreement?
I can engage the inspector now and hold any rebuild order until the report defines it.
I sketched next week's plan for the bid cycles before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the tender ledger updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Access to the depot is limited to the school break because the loading bay operates during term time.
Does the inspection timing matter?
Yes, missing it would postpone the evidence we need.
I compared two options for the site dossier tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the procurement room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Can I place the full depot roof rebuild order now?

replacement_dialogue.content: I filed the routine bid cycles paperwork and confirmed the owner list.
I did a standard pass over the site dossier records this morning.
The facilities lead has pencilled in an inspection window but says the report may not be used before tendering.
Would that support the same step?
No, without using the report, the rebuild scope remains untested.
